title: Log cabin square — textured
subtitle: Alternating htr and dc strips add a ridge texture to the log cabin construction
excerpt: Alternating half treble and double crochet strips across the log cabin square create a subtle ridge at every colour change. The htr strip sits slightly higher than the dc strip beside it, giving each pair a stepped profile visible from the side and a lined texture from above.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), textured strip motif chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A textured log cabin crochet square in two tones of dusty blue DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Alternating ridge lines visible across each strip pair, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished square measures 12 × 12 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Log cabin square — textured
chartDefinition.caption: Strips alternate dc (shorter) and htr (taller). Each pair of strips — one dc, one htr — forms a ridged band.

glossaryTerms.definition: A strip worked in half treble sits fractionally taller than an adjacent double crochet strip, creating a raised ridge line at the boundary between them.

content.text: Alternating dc and htr strips create a
at each colour change. The half treble is one step taller than the double crochet, and that height difference is enough to give a stepped profile visible in raking light.

Use two tones of the same colour family to keep the texture prominent without the distraction of a strong colour contrast. Two shades of the same blue or two neutrals work well; high contrast pulls the eye to the colour before the texture.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 6 g each of two tones of DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work the centre rectangle in dc (colour A). For each strip, alternate: one strip in htr (colour B), one strip in dc (colour A). Keep the strip width to 2 rows per strip. The height difference between stitch types means the outer edge stays level.
For a smoother texture, try the bavarian crochet square, which builds concentric rings with a post-stitch ridge rather than strip-by-strip construction.
